title: Expectations & evidence — Possible
description: Learn how Possible separates outputs, expectations, evidence, verification, and completion.

headings.text: The artifact is not the proof.

sections.heading: The four layers
sections.text: The four layers Keeping these terms separate prevents a polished deliverable from being mistaken for a completed outcome. OUTPUT The inspectable artifact EXPECTATION What must become true EVIDENCE What was observed or preserved VERIFICATION Why the claim can be trusted OUTPUT A responsive launch page with a working conversion flow. EXPECTATION The confirmed audience can complete the flow on supported screen sizes, approved claims are used, and accessibility checks pass.

sections.heading: Required and preferred expectations
sections.text: Required and preferred expectations A pack can include required and preferred checklist items. Each item is explicit and observable; no hidden module or domain-specific schema creates work outside the prompt, Skills, and Expectations. REQUIRED Completion blockers If an active required expectation fails, the run cannot honestly close. Preserve the failure, repair the result, and rerun the complete review. PREFERRED Quality signals Useful improvements that inform the completion report without pretending they are blockers when the approved contract did not require them.

sections.heading: What a complete review does
sections.text: What a complete review does Inspect the integrated artifact Review the result as one coherent outcome, not as isolated specialist handoffs. Challenge every active expectation Use the appropriate tests, measurements, review, or fixture and preserve the evidence used. Record failures and limitations Do not silently downgrade a failed check or turn an unproven claim into a success. Repair and rerun After a material repair, repeat the complete review so the new result is freshly verified.

sections.heading: Outcome Record
sections.text: Outcome Record Every run exposes one machine-readable Outcome Record. It connects the approved brief and pack snapshot to artifacts, hashes, expectation results, decisions, failures, repairs, approvals, limitations, and fresh verification. COMPLETION REPORT The final report says what was produced, what was checked, what remains unproven, and which external actions were intentionally not taken.
